text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices makes your API easier to use and maintain. First, choose clear and meaningful endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened — for example, 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, write good documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, such as /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. These simple rules help developers work with your API confidently and reduce confusion.
